clue.text: Demons in head of crying baby breaking most of hearts, say?

indicators.note: breaking says the trimmed card word is split open by the other pieces
most of means the last letter of the card word is dropped

parts.note: hearts is an example of a suit of cards

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word crying

parts.note: a cub is a baby animal

explanation.surface: A grisly scene of demons inside a wailing infant, with a coy question about broken hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts, say' names the card suit, and 'most of' drops its last letter before 'breaking' splits it open; the 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Succubi are female demons of folklore, so the plural noun matches 'Demons'.

clue.text: See 20
Hawk gripping tail of mynah bird

indicators.note: gripping means the throat-clearing word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: to hawk is to clear the throat noisily, to cough

indicators.note: tail of picks the last letter of the word mynah

explanation.surface: A bird of prey seizing a mynah by its tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning to cough; the definition is 'bird' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The chough is a crow-family bird with red legs and bill, found on sea cliffs.

clue.text: Free, served without cheese, might you say?

indicators.note: might you say signals that the made-up word is matched by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a dish served without feta, a Greek cheese, could jokingly be called un-feta-ed

explanation.surface: A diner noting that a salad came free, or came minus its cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Feta is a Greek cheese; 'un-feta-ed' is a coined word for a dish without it, and spoken it matches a real word.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfettered means not chained or restrained, so at liberty or free.

clue.text: Acquire lead-free metal, sure for shelling

indicators.note: lead-free means the metal loses its leading letter

parts.note: zinc is a metal

indicators.note: for shelling means the outer letters of the word sure are stripped off

explanation.surface: Advice on buying unleaded metal, said with confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead-free' looks like a property of the metal (no lead, Pb); it actually removes the first letter Z.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost or debt is to acquire it, usually as a result of one's own actions.

clue.text: Impetus lost, now stop

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and been jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Momentum has gone, so it is time to call a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the call that a period is over, telling people to stop now.

clue.text: Player was furious, I having taken bronze on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says the colour word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a bronze is a suntan, so tan
raged means was furious

explanation.surface: A sportsman, angry at only getting third place, with the bronze medal on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests a sportsman winning bronze; here it is an actor, and 'bronze' is a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who plays tragic roles, so a player on stage.

clue.text: Happen upon rabbit and duck etc in conversation?

indicators.note: in conversation means the word is as heard when spoken

parts.note: rabbit and duck are kinds of flesh you eat, so meat

explanation.surface: Coming across a rabbit and a duck having a chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' also means chat in British slang, adding to the false talk picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone can mean to come across them by chance, the same as happen upon.

clue.text: See 19
Items hanging down, butt appropriately covered?

indicators.note: covered means one piece sits inside the other, which wraps it

a butt is the end of something, as of a cigarette

explanation.surface: Something dangling, with a cheeky question about whether a bottom is decently clothed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clothing word is not printed; 'appropriately' hints that what suits a butt as a cover is pants, around END.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendants are ornaments hung from a chain or a ceiling, so things that hang down.

clue.text: Somewhat distant, a gull returning

indicators.note: returning means the dupe word is read backwards

parts.note: to gull is to dupe, and a gull is a dupe or fool

explanation.surface: A seagull flying back home, seen from far off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gull' is the dupe, not the seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof describes someone reserved and cool towards others, emotionally distant.

clue.text: Lizard finding pleasure ultimately in fruit, after drink

indicators.note: after says the fruit part follows the drink

parts.note: cha is a word for tea

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the fruit

parts.note: a melon is a fruit

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the word pleasure

explanation.surface: A lizard enjoying some fruit after a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The chameleon is a lizard famed for changing its skin colour.

clue.text: Mature, go in for work that's engaging

indicators.note: in says the age and go words go inside the word for for

parts.note: per means for, as in per head
to age is to mature
a go is a turn

explanation.surface: Advice to grow up and take on engaging work.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping book you cannot put down is called this, so an engaging work.

clue.text: One has trouble turning over bones

indicators.note: turning over means the trouble word is reversed

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to turn over a pile of bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The ilia are the two hip bones, plural of ilium.

clue.text: Keeping strike, escape beamer

indicators.note: keeping means the escape word holds the strike word inside it

parts.note: flight is an escape
to lash is to strike

explanation.surface: Holding a strike while escaping a beamer, a dangerous head-high cricket delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: A beamer is a cricket ball bowled at head height without bouncing; here it means something that beams light.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch gives out a beam of light, so it is jokingly a beamer.

clue.text: No centrality and no eccentricity?

indicators.note: eccentricity, oddness, suggests the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An abstract question about whether something lacks both a centre and oddness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentricity' plays on 'centrality': off-centre is the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal, a strong way of saying no.

clue.text: I appreciate that defamatory accusations put in register for student of religious law

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A Talmudist studies the Talmud, the body of Jewish civil and religious law.

clue.text: Unsuitable one tying up the little devil?

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
a roper is one who ties up with rope

explanation.surface: A question of whether trussing a mischievous child is the right thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as 'one tying up the little devil', which is an imp roper.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means unfit or not appropriate, the same as unsuitable.

clue.text: Polaris, say, swell for launch

parts.note: Polaris, the pole star, is an example of a star
a swell is a well-dressed upper-class person, a toff

explanation.surface: A Polaris missile and a surge of power for a launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polaris' evokes the submarine missile; 'swell' is a toff, a posh British type.
explanation.definitionFit: To start off a venture is to launch it, set it going.

clue.text: Dialogue as yet unmentioned in paper, nurturing quality

indicators.note: in says these words go inside the paper abbreviation

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, a written paper
other means not already mentioned, as in other things
an actor's lines are the dialogue

explanation.surface: A newspaper article whose dialogue hints at a caring trait.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the caring, protective nature of a mother, a nurturing quality.

clue.text: Tender thumps magnificent

parts.note: to pound is to thump
sterling means excellent, of the highest quality

explanation.surface: A tender spot being thumped magnificently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like sore; it is legal tender, money.
explanation.definitionFit: British currency is legal tender in the UK.

clue.text: Encourage crocodile, please — and quickly!

definitions.meaning: to urge a crocodile on is to tell it to be snappish, to snap its jaws
an impatient request to hurry up

explanation.surface: Urging a crocodile to get a move on, politely but impatiently.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a demand to hurry, and read literally tells a croc to be snappy.

clue.text: Odd choice

definitions.meaning: odd means unusual or seldom seen
choice means excellent, of fine quality

explanation.definitionFit: Rare means uncommon, and it also means unusually fine, as a rare vintage.

clue.text: Ladies and gentlemen in Florence possibly missing New York, a US city

missing means the state abbreviation is removed

the Ladies and the Gents are both public toilets, so loos

clue.text: Setter possibly making appearance in public, an idiot

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is the crossword setter in the surface; here it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A canid is any member of the dog family, and a setter is one breed of dog.

clue.text: Dogs, say, insulted every so often

indicators.note: every so often picks alternate letters of the word insulted

explanation.surface: Dogs, for instance, being insulted from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is a district of east London.

clue.text: Hack put on airs as lover of French writing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Proustian is an admirer of Marcel Proust, the French novelist.

clue.text: Kind politician, on having shifted to the far right

indicators.text: having shifted to the far right

parts.note: a Green is a member of the Green Party
re means on or about

clue.text: Quietly consider when judge allowed to detain criminal, originally

indicators.note: to detain says the allowed word holds that letter inside it

parts.note: let means allowed

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of the word criminal

clue.text: Stated floppy storing a digital file

floppy means loose and limp, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone said that a floppy disk stores a digital file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floppy' evokes the floppy disk; it is the anagram signal.
